$comment: Blueprint §8.1: 'A component may only reference tier 3.'
Why the third tier exists at all: tier 1 alone means a redesign edits every
component; tier 2 alone means a component cannot be adjusted without
affecting everything sharing its semantic token. Tier 3 gives per-component
escape hatches without leaking raw values upward — it is what turns a
year-six redesign into a token change rather than a rewrite.
Every value here references tier 2. A tier-1 reference in this file is a

component.$comment_metric: Metric values are text-primary in EVERY state. §8.2: 'health data is never coloured by valence. A mood of 2 is not red.' Deviation is communicated by position against a baseline, not by alarm colour.

chart.$comment: Missing data renders as a gap, never interpolated (§8.9 invariant 3). There is deliberately no 'missing data' colour token — a gap is an absence, not a value.

component.$comment_table: §8.11: 'On mobile, tables become card lists.' Both renderings are one DOM switched by a container query, so the card tokens below are the same table dressed differently rather than a second component's palette.

table.$comment_sticky: The sticky first column scrolls over the rows beside it, so it needs an opaque fill of its own — a transparent sticky cell smears the columns it passes.

component.$comment_listbox: Shared by ComboboxField and anything else that pops a list of options (§8.10). The active-option fill is accent-subtle rather than accent, because the option text stays text-primary and must keep its AAA ratio against it.
component.$comment_tag: TagField chips (§8.10). Neutral by construction — a tag is a label the operator chose, never a judgement about it (§8.2).
component.$comment_focus: A visible focus ring is required on every interactive element (§8.13). This token exists so it can never be styled away per-component.

skeleton.$comment: Skeletons hold layout; they do NOT shimmer (§8.6). Nothing animates on data load.
